fields.title: Management Training
fields.description:
Management training should assist participants to:
•	recognize evidence of personal predispositions in their employees that might make them inclined to respond to stressful events inappropriately
•	recognize and respond to concerning behaviours and concerning technical actions in their employees
•	recognize stressful events that were consequential in the cases studied and take mitigating actions
•	impose sanctions appropriately
•	monitor sanctioned employees for inappropriate reactions
•	understand when they may need to request assistance from qualified outsiders, including security and IT specialists, employee assistance officers, and mental health professionals, to fully evaluate risk
•	establish advanced security policies related to system administrators and technical or privileged users

fields.title: Management Training
fields.description:
Management training should assist participants to:
•	review and improve management practices to align resources with task
•	improve data flow by enhancing communication and maintaining accurate procedures
•	maintain a productive work setting by minimizing distractions
•	implement effective work planning and control to reduce job pressure and manage time factors
•	maintain employee readiness
•	maintain staff values and attitudes that align with organizational mission and ethics
•	implement security best practices throughout the organization

fields.title: Management Training
fields.description:
Management training should assist participants to:
•	enhance security awareness
•	divide responsibility for critical functions among employees
•	effectively separate duties (least privilege policy)
•	implement strict password and account management policies and practices
•	consider insider threats in the software development life cycle (SDLC)
•	deal effectively with workplace issues, beginning with pre-employment (agreements, clearly communicate responsibilities, etc.) and continuing through employment (workplace disputes, inappropriate relationships, etc.)

fields.title: Management Training
fields.description:
Management training should assist participants to:
•	raise awareness of the risks of insider threat
•	help identify the factors influencing an insider’s decision to act
•	help identify the indicators and precursors of malicious acts
•	identify countermeasures that will improve the survivability and resiliency of the organization

fields.title: Management Training
fields.description:
Management training should assist participants to:
•	comprehend the necessity of specific agreements being in place (IP ownership and consent to employee monitoring)
•	identify and properly label critical intellectual property (IP) assets
•	establish the necessary communication among departments dealing with insider threat

fields.title: Human Resources Training
fields.description:
Human Resources Training should assist participants to:
•	design a targeted monitoring strategy for employees and contractors dealing with critical IP assets of the organization
•	establish necessary nondisclosure agreements, IP ownership policies, and references to IP ownership in a network acceptable-use policy

fields.title: Human Resources Training
fields.description:
Human Resources Training should assist participants to:
•	provide emotional health counselling and stress reduction through Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) and workplace violence prevention programs 
•	provide support for employee fatigue or sleepiness through EAP support and workplace stress load reduction 
•	use positive framing rather than negative framing of problems to encourage less risky behaviour and more balanced decisions

fields.title: Human Resources Training
fields.description:
Human Resources Training should assist participants to:
•	establish policies related to observable signs of serious mental health disorders, personality problems, social skills and decision-making biases, and history of rule conflicts
•	comprehend sophisticated employee evaluation techniques 
•	familiarize with psychological assessments and their exploitation
•	handle dismissal procedures following proper and creative termination policies

fields.title: Human Resources Training
fields.description:
Human Resources Training should assist participants to:
•	clearly formulate employment agreements and conditions of employment
•	communicate responsibilities and constraints of each employee and consequences for violations 
•	effectively handle workplace disputes or inappropriate relationships between co-workers not to undermine a healthy and productive working environment
•	encourage discussion over work-related issues without fear of reprisal or negative consequences

fields.title: Security Awareness Training
fields.description:
Security Awareness Training should assist employees to:
•	recognize responsibility for reporting concerning behaviours and concerning technical actions to management
•	comprehend security policies and procedures tied to an organization’s mission, values, and critical assets
•	familiarize with separation of duties and remote access policies

fields.title: Security Awareness Training
fields.description:
Security Awareness Training should assist employees to:
•	enhance awareness of insider threat risks and impacts, including unintentional insider threat
•	heighten motivation to be wary of insider threat risks
•	train employees to recognize phishing and other social media threat vectors
•	engender process discipline to encourage adherence to policies and guidelines
•	train continuously to maintain proper level of knowledge, skills, and ability
•	conduct training on and improve awareness of risk perception and cognitive biases that affect decision making
•	improve human factors and usability of security tools.
•	improve usability of software to reduce likelihood of system-induced human error
•	identify potential actions or ways of thinking that could lead to an unintentional event, including:
	-	level of risk tolerance – someone willing to take more risks than the norm
	-	attempts at multi-tasking – individuals who multi-task may be more likely to make mistakes
	-	large amounts of personal or proprietary information shared on social media
	-	lack of attention to detail

fields.title: Security Awareness Training
fields.description:
Security Awareness Training should assist participants to:
•	enhance security awareness 
•	familiarize with good password and account management practices
•	identify malicious insiders by behaviour and not by stereotypical characteristics

fields.title: Security Awareness Training
fields.description:
Security Awareness Training should assist employees to:
•	understand the need for policies, procedures, and technical controls
•	familiarize with the security policies and procedures within the organization
•	become aware of consequences for security infractions 
•	understand that individuals, either inside or outside the organization, may try to co-opt them into activities that are counter to the organization’s mission, including committing fraud
•	understand the process for reporting policy violations

fields.title: Information Technology
fields.description:
Information Technology Training should assist participants to:
•	implement system change controls to prevent insertion of backdoors, keystroke loggers, logic bombs, and other malicious code or programs
•	log, monitor, and audit employee online actions so as to early discover and investigate suspicious insider actions
•	build layered defence against remote attacks

fields.title: Information Technology
fields.description:
Information Technology Training should assist participants to:
•	deactivate computer access following termination
•	implement secure backup and recovery processes

fields.title: Information Technology
fields.description:
Information Technology Training should assist participants to:
•	log, monitor, and audit employee online actions for at least 30 days prior to employee termination

fields.title: Security Awareness Training
fields.description:
Security Awareness Training should assist employees to:
•	understand the need for policies, procedures, and technical controls, along with their justification, implementation, and enforcement within the organization
•	become aware of individuals, either inside or outside the organization, who might try to co-opt them into activities counter to the organization’s mission
•	detect and report disruptive behavior by employees
•	monitor adherence to organizational policies and controls
•	monitor and control changes to organizational systems (e.g., to prevent the installation of malicious code) 
•	require separation of duties between employees who modify data and those who approve modifications
•	detect and report violations of the security of the organization’s facilities and physical assets
•	plan for potential incident response proactively

fields.title: Social Engineering Training
fields.description:
Social Engineering Training could be part of an organization’s security awareness training program. However, due to social media uprising trend, dedicated training program could assist in:
•	establishing, monitoring, and enforcing proper and legit social media policies
•	understanding data classification levels
•	outlining ways in which information exposed in social media may be used (including for potential recruitment into a crime organization or extremist groups)
•	comprehending what type of data can be collected from a randomly selected profile

fields.title: Customer Service Training
fields.description:
Training on reducing risks to customer service processes should focus on:
•	protecting computer accounts used in these processes
•	auditing access to customer records 
•	ensuring consistent enforcement of defined security policies and controls
•	implementing proper system administration safeguards for critical servers 
•	using secure backup and recovery methods to ensure availability of customer service data

fields.title: Refresher Training (annually)
fields.description:
Refresher Training needs to cover all facets of an organization, not just information security. Training should encompass the following topics: 
•	human resources
•	legal counsel
•	physical security, and 
•	any others of interest. 
Training can include, but should not be limited to:
•	changes to policies
•	issues that have emerged over the past year
•	information security trends

fields.title: Management Training
fields.description:
Management Training should assist participants to:
•	recognize and respond to inappropriate or concerning behavior in employees
•	consistently investigate and respond to all rule violations
•	monitor indications by employees of possible financial problems or unexplained financial gain.

fields.title: Human Resources Training
fields.description:
Human Resources Training should focus on:
•	the insider threat policies and the processes that address them across the organization
•	the foundation, maintenance, and constant enhancement of an employee assistance program (EAP)

fields.title: Legal Counsel
fields.description:
Legal Counsel Training should focus on: 
•	reviewing insider threat policies 
•	analyzing issues that arose in the past year 
•	outlining strategies to avoid similar incidents in the future

fields.title: Physical Security
fields.description:
Physical Security Training should focus on:
•	reviewing policies and procedures for access to company facilities by employees, contractors, and trusted business partners
•	reviewing any policies on prohibited devices (USB devices, cameras, etc.)
•	proper handling of the organization’s physical assets as well as evacuation or emergency procedures that may arise in the event of an emergency

fields.title: Data owners
fields.description:
Data Owners Training should focus on:
•	discussing projects that may have heightened risk of insider threat, for example, strategic research projects that will involve creation of new trade secrets
•	identifying the value of an organization’s IP (Intellectual Property) and the potential damage associated with an insider attack

fields.title: Information Technology
fields.description:
Information Technology Training should focus on:
•	efficiently educating employees on procedures for recognizing viruses and other malicious code
•	identifying which devices should be prohibited or permitted for authorized use on the various information systems within the organization

fields.title: Software Engineering
fields.description: Software Engineering Training should focus on effective auditing of configuration management logs to detect insertion of malicious code
